_note: Annex III AI Act (high-risk use cases), simplified. A system listed here is high-risk unless the Article 6(3) derogation applies (and never if it performs profiling of natural persons). Not legal advice.

areas.name: Biometrics (insofar as permitted by law)
use_cases: 1(a) remote biometric identification systems (NOT biometric verification whose only purpose is to confirm that a person is who they claim to be)
1(b) biometric categorisation according to sensitive or protected attributes
1(c) emotion recognition systems
examples: identifying people in a crowd from CCTV after the fact
emotion recognition in a customer call centre

areas.name: Critical infrastructure
use_cases: 2 safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or the supply of water, gas, heating or electricity
examples: an AI system that controls valves in a water distribution network

areas.name: Education and vocational training
use_cases: 3(a) determining access or admission, or assigning people to educational institutions
3(b) evaluating learning outcomes, including when used to steer the learning process
3(c) assessing the appropriate level of education a person will receive or can access
3(d) monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour of students during tests

areas.name: Employment, workers management and access to self-employment
use_cases: 4(a) recruitment or selection: placing targeted job ads, analysing and filtering applications, evaluating candidates
4(b) decisions affecting work relationships (promotion, termination), allocating tasks based on behaviour or personal traits, monitoring and evaluating performance and behaviour of workers
examples: an algorithm assigning shifts to delivery riders based on their ratings

areas.name: Access to essential private and public services and benefits
use_cases: 5(a) public authorities evaluating eligibility for public assistance benefits and services (including healthcare), or granting, reducing or revoking them
5(b) evaluating creditworthiness or establishing a credit score (EXCEPT systems used to detect financial fraud)
5(c) risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance
5(d) evaluating and classifying emergency calls, dispatching emergency services, emergency healthcare patient triage

areas.name: Law enforcement (insofar as permitted by law)
use_cases: 6(a) assessing the risk of a person becoming a victim of crime
6(b) polygraphs and similar tools
6(c) evaluating the reliability of evidence
6(d) assessing the risk of offending or re-offending not solely based on profiling, or assessing personality traits or past criminal behaviour
6(e) profiling of people during the detection, investigation or prosecution of crimes
examples: a tool estimating the reliability of witness statements for police

areas.name: Migration, asylum and border control management (insofar as permitted by law)
use_cases: 7(a) polygraphs and similar tools
7(b) assessing security, irregular migration or health risks posed by a person entering a Member State
7(c) assisting the examination of applications for asylum, visas and residence permits, including the reliability of evidence
7(d) detecting, recognising or identifying people in this context (EXCEPT verification of travel documents)
examples: a system scoring visa applications for risk

areas.name: Administration of justice and democratic processes
use_cases: 8(a) assisting a judicial authority (or alternative dispute resolution) in researching and interpreting facts and law, and applying the law to facts
8(b) influencing the outcome of an election or referendum or people's voting behaviour (EXCEPT tools whose output people are not directly exposed to, e.g. tools to organise campaigns logistically)
examples: a tool suggesting sentences to judges
micro-targeting political ads to change voting behaviour
